extraction.name: EgoLife Dataset
extraction.description: A comprehensive 300-hour egocentric, interpersonal, multiview, and multimodal daily life dataset featuring six participants living together for one week, continuously recording their daily activities using AI glasses for multimodal egocentric video capture, along with synchronized third-person-view video references.
extraction.creator: The EgoLife Team
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Six participants lived together for one week in a custom-designed environment (EgoHouse), wearing Meta Aria glasses to capture multimodal egocentric videos. Each participant recorded a minimum of six hours per day during waking hours. Activities included discussions, shopping, cooking, socializing, entertainment, and preparing for an Earth Day celebration. 15 strategically placed GoPro cameras recorded third-person perspectives, and millimeter-wave radars provided spatial and motion data.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Direct measurement, Physical data collection, Software Collection, Passive Data Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data sources include: (1) Egocentric video, audio, IMU, and gaze data from Meta Aria glasses worn by six participants; (2) Third-person video from 15 GoPro cameras; (3) Spatial and motion data from two mmWave devices (TI IWR6843 60GHz radars with DCA1000 data capture boards); (4) For Milan subset: WiFi signal data from three Asus RT-AX82U devices using AX-CSI platform.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Seven days for Beijing dataset; one day for Milan dataset
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Recordings were structured into three-hour segments due to storage limitations. Glasses were collected every three hours for data upload and storage clearance (approximately one hour). During this period, participants were instructed to remain in their rooms and limit activities to resting or non-essential tasks to prevent logic disruptions in recorded footage.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Data preprocessing included: (1) Multi-source data synchronization using EgoSync codebase to align video, audio, and IMU data from Aria glasses and GoPro cameras using timestamps; (2) Privacy protection through EgoBlur module - all participant faces were blurred, bystanders' faces and vehicle license plates were blurred, sensitive audio segments were muted, and screens displaying private information were masked; (3) Video splitting into 5-minute clips slowed to 0.8x speed for annotation; (4) Audio processing for transcript generation; (5) mmWave signal processing using constant false alarm rate (CFAR) detection algorithm; (6) WiFi CSI data extraction (2048 subcarriers × 16 spatial streams per frame).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations were created in multiple stages: (1) Transcript annotations: Speech recognition applied to merged audio from six participants, followed by diarization to differentiate speakers, then human review for accuracy with audio split into six tracks per participant; (2) Caption annotations: Annotators provided continuous detailed narrations for 5-minute video clips at 0.8x speed, covering all actions, interactions, and environmental details. Narrations were converted to text via transcription tool, then reviewed and corrected. Initial 361K brief narrations (averaging 2.65 seconds) were merged into 25K coherent captions using GPT-4o-mini, then expanded into visual-audio captions by pairing with representative frames (1 FPS) and transcripts, summarized by GPT-4o and verified by human annotators; (3) QA annotations: GPT-4o generated approximately 100K timestamped questions per participant from visual-audio captions. Annotators viewed questions synced with video segments, filtering for questions requiring information from at least five minutes prior. Final curation resulted in 500 QA per participant (3K total) with human-generated distractors for multiple-choice format.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: CapCut (ByteDance) for video captioning; Speech recognition and diarization algorithms for transcripts; GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini for caption enhancement and QA generation
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Questions were annotated with: (1) Whether audio was required to answer; (2) Certification length (look-back time) necessary for retrieving correct answer, categorized into four levels: <2h, 2h-6h, 6h-24h, >24h. Only questions requiring information from at least five minutes prior were retained, with preference for longer dependencies and strong real-world relevance.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Multiple levels of annotations per video segment: (1) 361K initial narrations averaging 2.65 seconds each; (2) 25K merged captions; (3) Visual-audio captions with 1 FPS frame sampling; (4) 500 QA pairs per participant (3K total) after filtering from 100K AI-generated candidates
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Whisper Large v3 for speech recognition; Open-source diarization algorithm for speaker differentiation; GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini for caption merging, enhancement, and QA generation; CFAR detection algorithm for mmWave signal processing
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The project is ongoing with plans to expand the dataset to cover a broader range of languages, locations, and activities. A one-day English-language subset (EgoLife-Milan) has been collected in Milan, Italy. Future versions will be detailed in upcoming EgoLife blog series.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset involves six participants living together, capturing daily activities including personal interactions, conversations, and behaviors. All participant faces were blurred for anonymization. Bystanders' faces and vehicle license plates were also blurred. Sensitive audio segments containing private or potentially identifiable information were muted. Screens displaying passwords or personal data were masked.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The EgoLife project aims to develop egocentric life assistants that enhance personal efficiency through AI-powered wearable glasses, offering personalized assistance in daily life. Potential positive impacts include improved quality of life for individuals needing consistent support (elderly, those with cognitive challenges), facilitation of learning and task tracking in educational/professional settings. The technology could foster meaningful human-AI interactions. However, deep integration into personal spaces raises privacy concerns requiring safeguards for data privacy, user autonomy, and transparency in AI decision-making.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is limited by: (1) Primary language is Chinese for the main 7-day dataset, limiting generalizability across languages; (2) Single location/scenario (shared house in Beijing for main dataset), sacrificing some generalizability; (3) Limited to six participants over one week; (4) Activities centered around preparing for an Earth Day celebration may not represent all daily life scenarios; (5) Recording structured into 3-hour segments with 1-hour breaks may create discontinuities; (6) Current models show limitations in speech understanding (struggles with laughter and emotions), identity recognition (overfitting to early observations), and lack of multi-step reasoning in retrieval.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset supports multiple use cases: (1) Training: EgoIT-99K instruction-tuning dataset for training EgoGPT model; Fine-tuning on EgoLife Day-1 data for personalization; (2) Evaluation: EgoLifeQA benchmark for long-context, life-oriented question-answering tasks including EntityLog (object memory), EventRecall (past events), HabitInsight (personal patterns), RelationMap (interpersonal interactions), and TaskMaster (task assignment); (3) Research applications: Long-term behavior pattern analysis, social interaction dynamics, multimodal egocentric video understanding, ultra-long-context (week-level) question answering, identity recognition and tracking, ego-exo alignment studies, spatial cognition from egocentric video.
